currency: Moroccan dirham (de facto), Sahrawi peseta (Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic)

landmarks.name: Dakhla Peninsula
landmarks.writeup: A prominent peninsula known for its desert landscapes and Atlantic coastline, popular for water sports and fishing.

landmarks.name: Smara
landmarks.writeup: An important town with historical significance as a center of Islamic scholarship and Sahrawi culture.

landmarks.name: Laayoune
landmarks.writeup: The largest city and administrative center, featuring markets and cultural sites reflecting Sahrawi heritage.

head_of_state: Brahim Ghali (President of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic, partially recognized)

cultural_events.name: Sahrawi National Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on February 27, marking the founding of the Polisario Front and the Sahrawi struggle for independence.

cultural_events.name: Eid al-Fitr
cultural_events.writeup: A major Islamic festival celebrated by Sahrawi people marking the end of Ramadan with communal prayers and feasts.

food_writeup: Sahrawi cuisine is influenced by Berber, Arab, and Spanish traditions, featuring dishes like mechoui (roasted lamb), couscous, and tea ceremonies with mint tea.
brief_history: Western Sahara was a Spanish colony until 1975. Following Spain's withdrawal, Morocco and Mauritania claimed the territory, leading to conflict with the Polisario Front, which declared the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic. The region remains disputed with ongoing tensions and a UN-brokered ceasefire since 1991.

important_people.name: Brahim Ghali
important_people.description: Current President of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic

important_people.name: Mohamed Abdelaziz
important_people.description: Longtime leader of the Polisario Front

current_conflicts: Ongoing territorial dispute between Morocco and the Polisario Front over sovereignty, with intermittent clashes despite a UN ceasefire.
